creator: Alexander Terp
description: After a_32xpBgrr9 pointer input no longer counts toward stuck. On Linux FIONREAD sees only the line discipline's 4,095 bytes while the pty's flip buffer takes far more, so a program that hangs with keys unread is not read stuck while 4 KiB or more of pointer reports sit behind those keys, until the next key. Two bounds were tried in a raw Linux PTY while building that card and both failed: a 2 KiB FIONREAD check before each pointer write let 6,001 bytes through when a held batch drained at once (Writer::pace holds mouse events during key gaps), and a 1 KiB writer-side budget refilled on an empty FIONREAD let 4,095 or more through in 81 of 10,000 batches, because an empty sample also omits the flip buffer. Untried: a budget whose refill is also rate-limited (at most one refill per tens of milliseconds), or not holding pointer events for a batch drain. The measurements are in that card's commit message. Raised by factory run muster-1119-iris.
title: Bound pointer input queued behind unread keys so Linux can still read a hung program stuck
